Science Lab / MAKE · LEARN · DISCOVER

Grow a bean.

A tiny seed. A whole lot to discover.

Ages 6–1220 min + daily check-insIndoors

A clear container lets you look at the part of a plant that usually hides underground. Set up a bean, make a prediction, and return each day to see what has changed. Germination can take several days; every seed has its own pace.

BEFORE YOU BEGIN

Gather your bits.

Tick things off as you get ready.

A note for grown-ups

An adult should help set up and supervise. Seeds are a choking hazard: keep them away from younger children and never eat the seeds or sprouts. Wash hands afterward. An adult should discard any mouldy seeds without children handling them.

A little more guidance ↗
ONE STEP AT A TIME

Let's make it happen.

  1. Wake up the seeds

    Soak the bean seeds in water overnight, then drain. Prepare two or three so you can compare them; some seeds may not sprout.

  2. Make a window for the roots

    Dampen a folded paper towel and place it against the inside of the container. It should feel damp, not drip. Tuck the beans between the towel and the container wall so you can see them.

  3. Choose a place and predict

    Stand the open container in a warm spot with indirect daylight, away from a hot windowsill. Draw the beans and predict what will appear first. Label the date.

  4. Look a little every day

    Check once a day. Add a spoonful of water if the towel is drying out, and tip out standing water. Draw any changes. Once a root appears, measure it gently through the container; do not pull the bean out.

  5. Give your seedling a new home

    When roots and leaves have developed, ask an adult to help transplant the seedling into potting soil. Keep the shoot above the soil. Continue observing in a bright place and water as needed.

THE LITTLE BIT OF LEARNING

What's happening here?

Water allows the seed to start germinating. The first root anchors the seedling and takes up water; a shoot grows upward. Stored food in the seed supports early growth. Once leaves develop, light helps the plant make its own food.

Keep the wondering going.

  • What changed first: the seed coat, root or shoot?
  • Did every bean grow at the same speed?
  • What could you measure in the same way each day?

Make it work for you.

Keep it simple

An adult can write down a child's spoken observations. Draw just one bean each day.

Take it further

Measure the root at the same time each day and graph its length. Keep the light, seed type and amount of water consistent.

Not quite going to plan?

No change after about a week? Check that the towel stays damp and the spot is warm. Try fresh seeds if needed. A bad smell or fuzzy growth means an adult should discard the setup and start again with a clean container.
